chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Hamza, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said:

From the character of the believer is spending according to the level of need, and expanding (spending) according to the level of capacity, and being fair to people, and initiating them with the greeting of peace upon them.
ai.seo_question: What are the key moral characteristics and social etiquettes of a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Imam al-Baqir (AS), defines the moral character of the believer by linking financial prudence with social grace. It emphasizes that generosity must be calibrated to one's means while ensuring fairness, and it underscores the importance of proactive social engagement through initiating the greeting of peace, reflecting the Shia emphasis on communal harmony and humility.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik Bin Atiyya, from Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘From the mannerisms of the Momin is the spending upon a measurement of the standard of living, and being capacious upon a measurement of the capacity, and fairness to the people, and initiating them with the greetings upon them’.
en.sarwar: 36. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Malik ibn ‘Atiyyah from abu Hamza from Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) who has said the following: “

It is of the moral behavior of believers to spend proportionately to their standard of living, raise such standards to what is possible, fairness to people and initiation in offering the greeting of peace.”
